paragraphs: Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat.

His father, Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, was very dear to Rav, as in [Bava Batra 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.8b.14), where Rav applied to him the verse "and those who lead the many to righteousness shall be like the stars forever and ever."

Hyman writes that his son Rav Yehudah, apparently, also merited to receive from Rav; although Hyman does not find anywhere that he spoke with him face to face, he does find in several places that he said teachings in Rav's name, as in [Berakhot 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.47a.4), [48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.48a.4); [Shabbat 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.30b.3), [118b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118b.2) (and the same attribution should be corrected at [119b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.119b.6)), [153a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.153a.2); [Eruvin 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.14b.16-18) and [97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.97a.5); [Sukkah 46b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.46b.14); [Taanit 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.14a.7) and [29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.29b.2); [Megillah 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.5a.3); [Moed Katan 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.16a.11-12); [Yevamot 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.64b.3); [Menachot 35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.35b.7). In [Taanit 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.14a.7) he disagrees with Rav Yehudah. In [Moed Katan 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.16a.11-12), Rav Huna bar Chinena quotes Rav Chisda to him. In [Eruvin 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.14b.16-18), Rav Yosef reports a teaching that Rav Yehudah gave in Shmuel’s name. In Rav Rachumi’s version, Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat gives it in Rav’s name. Hyman takes the alternate version to clarify the attribution earlier in the passage.[^3] He is also mentioned in [Eruvin 85b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.85b.11) and [Yoma 76b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.76b.8).

notes.text: The notice retains both Shabbat118b and119b. Its proposed attribution correction at119b is not a replacement of118b.

The consulted Shabbat 118b directly names Yehudah son of Shmuel bar Shilat reporting Rav. Hyman’s proposed attribution correction at 119b remains separate from that 118b occurrence; his tentative personal contact and absence of a recorded face-to-face exchange remain his argument.

[Shabbat 118b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118b.2) gives Rav Yehudah without the patronymic; [119b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.119b.6) gives Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel, without bar Shilat. [Seder HaDorot 1678](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1678&lang=en) discusses the fuller form and cites [Eruvin 97a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.97a.5), the location of the tefillin-knot teaching Hyman lists at 96a.
